newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle end mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle end mostly higher.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures ended mostly higher with ideas that fed cattle prices have reached a near-term bottom providing strength, traders said.

Live cattle ended 0.550 cent per lb higher to 0.150 lower with June up most and August up 0.300 at 63.825 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.525 cent a lb higher to 0.250 lower with August up most at 77.275 cents.

Short covering sparked by expectations the fed cattle market has bottomed buoyed live cattle futures into the close despite late profit taking. Expectations are that cash will hold at least at $63 per cwt next week, traders said.

Cash cattle may have put in a seasonal bottom or are near their bottom and the outlook is for much stronger cash markets later in the year. Also, cash beef is expected to firm late this week or next after falling to lowest levels since February, they said.

However, some sources noted that before prices can rise significantly, packers will have abundant cattle numbers to work through this summer, possibly into early fall. They cited historically large and possibly record numbers of cattle on feed June 1.

Analyst estimates on USDA's monthly Cattle on Feed report to be released Friday put June 1 total on-feed supplies in the major seven states at an average of 113.2 percent of a year ago in a range of 111.5 to 114 percent. A number at the high end would be a record high.
May placement estimates averaged 117.2 percent of a year earlier in a range of 110.5 to 124 percent and marketing estimates averaged 99 percent in a range of 97 to 100.5.
Also, boxed beef prices fell another $1.02 to $0.48 per cwt at midday, with heavyweight choice down to $98.61, lowest level since February 20.
R.J. O'Brien bought June and August. Lind-Waldock bought June early. RBH notably bought August early before Refco sold late. Cargill Investor Services sold June and October late, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, a commission house was actively doing a covered risk reversal, buying October 66 puts and selling October 70 calls and October 62 puts, pit sources added.

The runup in live cattle and expectations of strong fed cattle prices later as well as expected lower feed costs ignited demand in feeder cattle futures. Prices rallied from early lows following recent weakness in the CME feeder cattle index and higher corn futures Wednesday, traders said.
The technical reversal on Tuesday and consolidation ahead of the Cattle-on-Feed report also provided support, they said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.30 at $77.28 per cwt.

Local buying boosted futures into buy stops before further spreading by Cargill limited the advance in August and September. Cargill spread long December live cattle/short August feeders and long February live cattle short September feeders. Rosenthal Collins bought August early, pit sources said.
